answer: A TCP SYN Flood attack works by sending a high volume of SYN (synchronize) packets to a target system, which can overwhelm the system and lead to a denial of service (DoS). This attack exploits the TCP handshake process, where the attacker sends numerous SYN requests but does not complete the handshake, causing the target to allocate resources for these half-open connections. As a result, the availability and functionality of the targeted system may be significantly reduced due to resource exhaustion [Source 1].
